evidence: src/application/CatalogueService.ts addProduct: `this.products.save(product);` after creating a Product, so product state is persisted through the repository.
src/application/OrderService.ts placeOrder: calls `product.reserve(item.quantity)` but never `this.products.save(product)`, while it does call `this.orders.save(order)`.
src/application/OrderService.ts cancelOrder: calls `product.release(line.quantity)` with no `products.save`, while it does call `this.orders.save(order)`.

src/application/OrderService.ts: `if (!product) throw new DomainError(`Product ${...} was not found`)` is repeated in placeOrder and cancelOrder, while the order lookup is put in one place in `private getOrder(id)`.
src/application/OrderService.ts placeOrder catch block: `this.products.findById(item.productId)?.release(...)` silently skips missing products, a third inconsistent version of the lookup rule.
src/application/OrderDtos.ts: `{ readonly productId: string; readonly quantity: number }` is written inline in both CreateOrderInput and OrderDto, and again in OrderService.combineItems.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The three files form one cohesive application layer: `CatalogueService` and `OrderService` are the use-case services, and `OrderDtos` holds their input and output contracts. Splitting the concerns is not the problem; how `OrderService` uses the persistence abstraction is.

**Inconsistent repository use.** `CatalogueService.addProduct` saves products through `ProductRepository.save`. `OrderService` saves the `Order` after every change (`placeOrder`, `advanceOrder`, `cancelOrder` all call `orders.save(order)`). But it changes `Product` stock with `product.reserve(...)` and `product.release(...)` in `placeOrder`, in the rollback branch and in `cancelOrder`, and never calls `products.save(product)`. Stock changes are only kept if the repository happens to return live in-memory objects. This bypasses the repository contract the module uses everywhere else.

**Duplicated rule.** `OrderService` puts the order lookup and its "not found" error in one helper, `getOrder`. The product lookup has no such helper: the same `findById` plus `DomainError('Product ... was not found')` is written inline in both `placeOrder` and `cancelOrder`. The rollback loop applies a different, silent rule for the same lookup (`findById(...)?.release`).

**Minor issues.** The item shape `{ productId; quantity }` is written out inline in `CreateOrderInput`, `OrderDto` and `OrderService.combineItems` instead of being one shared type. Product DTOs live in a file named `OrderDtos`.

The persistence bypass and the repeated lookup rule are the reasons for failing.

violations.message: Changes Product stock via reserve()/release() in placeOrder and cancelOrder but never saves products through ProductRepository.save. Orders are saved after every change, and CatalogueService saves products, so this bypasses the repository abstraction and relies on in-memory reference behaviour.

The product lookup and its 'Product ... was not found' DomainError are repeated inline in placeOrder and cancelOrder, and the rollback silently skips missing products, while the equivalent order rule lives in one helper (getOrder). The lookup rule should live in one place.
